(1) the nucleotide composition of a sequence is the most important factor in determining expression, (2) the nucleotide sequence of a gene can be optimized for protein expression, and (3) the optimal sequence depends on the host and the protein.

(i) the most important factors affecting expression are codon bias and mRNA secondary structure, (ii) the most important codon biases are the codon bias in the organism, and the codon bias for the protein being expressed, and (iii) the most important mRNA secondary structures are those that are thermodynamically favored and those that are predicted to affect translation.

(i) the sequence context of the first nucleotide of a codon has a large effect on the efficiency of translation of that codon, (ii) the effect of this context is not the same for all codons and (iii) the effect of context can be predicted by a simple model.
